My family has farmed this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know what grows here — the soil, the water table, the seasons. I have no paper learning, but I know this land with my hands.

Every year is the same for me, and that is not a bad thing. I grow **winter wheat** and then **summer maize** on the same fields. One plot, two crops, one year. That is what my father did. The wheat goes in around Hanlu (寒露) in October. The corn goes in the day after the wheat is cut in June. No gap, no wasted season. It works.

I rent about 10 mu total. I keep 1 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, some eggplant — for the family and sometimes sell a little at the village market.

For seeds, I buy from the village seed shop in town. For corn, I always buy hybrid —郑单958 or whatever they have that season. The yield is clearly better, everyone switched years ago. For wheat, I buy the improved variety the shopkeeper recommends, the same one I've used the past few years.

Fertilizer — I apply base fertilizer before sowing: one bag of diammonium phosphate and one bag of urea per mu, mixed in. Then I top-dress urea at jointing stage for wheat, and again for corn when it's knee-high. I know some village officials say we use too much, but I have seen what happens when you use too little.

For water, I pump from my own well. Wheat needs water badly — I pump at overwintering, green-up, jointing, and heading. Four times. Corn catches the summer rains mostly, I pump once if July is dry.

Pesticides — I spray wheat twice: once for weeds in spring, once for aphids. Corn once, for armyworm if I see it.

Tillage — I use the village tractor service for rotary tillage before wheat. For corn, I just seed directly into the wheat stubble, no tilling needed.
